title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy Form: Water Damage Exclusions and Limitations
content:
Water losses under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy are classified by the cause of loss recorded on the claim. Each cause below carries its own terms.

## 1. Sudden and accidental discharge; freeze — clause no longer in force

The following clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current settlement basis: "Damage from a sudden and accidental discharge of water, and freeze damage, settle under the loss settlement conditions with the all-other-perils deductible."

## 2. Continuous or repeated seepage or leakage

Damage from continuous or repeated seepage or leakage of water lasting the package's seepage exclusion days or more (the repeated seepage cause of loss) is excluded, with one exception: dwelling damage from a leak hidden inside walls, floors or ceilings is paid as **hidden water** coverage, up to the package's hidden water limit per term.

- On a package whose hidden water limit is 0, the whole seepage loss is denied as repeated seepage.
- The deteriorated plumbing itself is always denied as wear and tear.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical).* With a hypothetical seepage exclusion period of 14 days: seepage that lasted 14 days reaches the exclusion; seepage that lasted 13 days falls short of it and is not excluded by this clause.

## 3. Water backup and sump discharge

Water that backs up through sewers or drains or overflows a sump (the water backup cause of loss) is paid as **water backup** coverage only when the policy's water backup limit is above 0, up to that limit per occurrence after the all-other-perils deductible. With no water backup limit it is denied as no water backup coverage.

## 4. Fungi, wet rot and bacteria — clause no longer in force

The following clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current settlement basis: "Fungi, wet rot and bacteria remediation that results from a covered water loss is paid as mold coverage up to the package's mold limit in aggregate per term, measured by the term sublimit paid."

## 5. Per-term sublimits

Once a per-term sublimit is used up, further amounts under it are denied as sublimit exhausted.

The **term sublimit paid** for one sublimited coverage part, hidden water or mold, is the total of the claim payments of that part on the policy whose date of loss falls in the policy term containing the date of loss (from the term effective date through the expiration date), less the voided amounts of those payments.

- The hidden water limit remaining is the package's hidden water limit less the hidden water term sublimit paid.
- The mold limit remaining is the package's mold limit less the mold term sublimit paid.

*Hypothetical figures.* A hidden water limit of 10000 USD, with hidden water payments of 7500 USD in the term of which 1000 USD was voided: the term sublimit paid is 6500 USD and 3500 USD remains. When the term sublimit paid reaches the full 10000 USD, further hidden water amounts in that term are denied as sublimit exhausted.

## 6. Withheld depreciation on water payments — clause no longer in force

The following clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current settlement basis: "Holdback applies to hidden water, water backup and mold payments exactly as to the dwelling under the loss settlement conditions."

## Denial reasons at a glance

| Circumstance | Denial reason |
|---|---|
| Seepage loss on a package with no hidden water limit | Repeated seepage |
| Deteriorated plumbing | Wear and tear |
| Backup or sump overflow with no water backup limit | No water backup coverage |
| Per-term sublimit used up | Sublimit exhausted |

superseded_clauses: water_sudden_accidental and freeze damage settle under home_claim_settlement with the aop_deductible.
Fungi, wet rot and bacteria remediation that results from a covered water loss is paid as coverage_part mold up to mold_limit in aggregate per term, measured by home_msr_term_sublimit_paid.
Holdback applies to hidden_water, water_backup and mold payments exactly as to dwelling under home_claim_settlement.
